questions.explanation: In reported speech, present simple moves back to past simple: 'is' → 'was'.
questions.q: She said she ___ tired.

questions.explanation: Present simple becomes past simple in reported speech.
questions.q: 'I live in Madrid,' he said. → He said he ___ in Madrid.

questions.explanation: Present continuous becomes past continuous in reported speech.
questions.q: 'I'm working late,' she said. → She said she ___ late.

questions.explanation: Present perfect becomes past perfect in reported speech.
questions.q: 'I've finished,' he said. → He said he ___.

questions.explanation: 'Will' becomes 'would' in reported speech.
questions.q: 'I'll call you,' she said. → She said she ___ me.

questions.explanation: 'Can' becomes 'could' in reported speech.
questions.q: 'I can swim,' he said. → He said he ___ swim.

questions.explanation: With a past reporting verb, shift the tense back: 'am' → 'was'.
options: She said she was happy yesterday.
She said she will be happy yesterday.
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?

questions.explanation: Past simple becomes past perfect in reported speech.
questions.q: 'We saw the film,' they said. → They said they ___ the film.

questions.explanation: 'Must' usually becomes 'had to' in reported speech.
questions.q: 'I must go,' he said. → He said he ___ go.

questions.explanation: 'Going to' becomes 'was going to' in reported speech.
questions.q: 'I'm going to travel,' she said. → She said she ___ travel.

questions.explanation: Present simple negative becomes past simple: 'don't like' → 'didn't like'.
questions.q: 'I don't like coffee,' he said. → He said he ___ coffee.

questions.explanation: 'Will' becomes 'would' in reported speech.
questions.q: 'We'll be late,' they said. → They said they ___ late.

questions.explanation: Present perfect becomes past perfect in reported speech.
questions.q: 'I have lived here for years,' she said. → She said she ___ there for years.

questions.explanation: 'May' becomes 'might' in reported speech.
questions.q: 'I may come,' he said. → He said he ___ come.

questions.explanation: With a past reporting verb, don't keep the present tense: 'was', not 'is'.
options: He said he is tired yesterday.
questions.q: Which sentence is WRONG?

questions.explanation: Present continuous for future becomes past continuous: 'was leaving'.
questions.q: 'I'm leaving tomorrow,' she said. → She said she ___ the next day.

questions.explanation: Past simple becomes past perfect in reported speech.
questions.q: 'I bought a car,' he said. → He said he ___ a car.

questions.explanation: 'Can't' becomes 'couldn't' in reported speech.
questions.q: 'We can't come,' they said. → They said they ___ come.

questions.explanation: Use 'told me' (not 'said me') and backshift the tense.
options: She said me she was ill.
She told me she was ill.
She said to me that she is ill.
questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?

questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous becomes past perfect continuous.
questions.q: 'I've been waiting,' he said. → He said he ___ waiting.
